backlog.title: Implement the +body format modifier (message-role prompt surface)
backlog.description: A single cohesive phase: implement the v3.4 spec change — an optional +body suffix on every --format base that forces a subject-plus-body message regardless of repo history shape. Grammar parsing + validation + prompt assembly, with tests and user-facing docs riding along. No commit/CAS/rescue/lock/provider touch. Message-role prompt surface only.

milestones.title: Core: grammar parsing, validation, prompt assembly
milestones.description: Implement the <base>[+body] grammar end-to-end through the format subsystem: splitFormat parser, bodyForceDirective constant, forceBody threading through buildFormatSystemPrompt/BuildSystemPrompt/BuildFallbackPrompt/BuildPlannerSystemPrompt, validateFormat extension, and the inline user-facing config-template/--help text.

tasks.title: +body grammar parsing + prompt assembly + inline doc/flag-help updates
tasks.description: Implement the <base>[+body] grammar end-to-end through the format subsystem, plus the user-facing config-template and --help text. The body-forcing directive replaces the multi-line rule; the subject scaffold is unchanged. The splitFormat parser is created in format.go and consumed by system.go, load.go, and planner.go.

subtasks.title: format.go + planner.go: add splitFormat parser + bodyForceDirective constant + thread forceBody through buildFormatSystemPrompt + fix planner base-dispatch
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/021_086bbc57a2b2/architecture/format_subsystem.md. The file internal/prompt/format.go currently has NO format-parsing logic — formatScaffoldBody(format) and buildFormatSystemPrompt(format, hasMultiline, subjectTarget) both use the raw format string. Constants conventionalScaffold, gitmojiScaffoldInstruction, multilineRuleAllow, multilineRuleSingle, promptPreamble are defined WITHOUT trailing newlines (package convention — callers own inter-block newline placement).
2. INPUT: No upstream subtask dependency — this is the parser origin point. The existing constants (multilineRuleAllow, multilineRuleSingle, promptPreamble, conventionalScaffold, gitmojiScaffoldInstruction) are available in format.go. RenderGitmojiTable() is available in gitmoji.go.
3. LOGIC:
   (a) Add `bodyForceDirective` const to format.go — VERBATIM from PRD §17.8 / Design Decision 4: `ALWAYS follow the subject with a body — a blank line, then a wrapped (~72-column) explanation of what this change does and why. Use a short bullet list only when the change has several distinct parts. The subject above still follows its format contract.` NO trailing newline (package convention).
   (b) Add `splitFormat(format string) (base string, forceBody bool)` to format.go: returns (format, false) when format has no "+body" suffix; returns (base, true) when format == base + "+body" exactly (case-sensitive on the suffix; the suffix "+body" must be the trailing 5 chars). Caller validates base.
   (c) Modify `buildFormatSystemPrompt(format string, hasMultiline bool, subjectTarget int)` — keep the SAME signature. Internally: `base, forceBody := splitFormat(format)`. Call `formatScaffoldBody(base)` (NOT raw format — subject contract keyed on base). When forceBody is true, write bodyForceDirective INSTEAD OF the multilineRuleAllow/multilineRuleSingle selection (the if/else on hasMultiline is skipped entirely). When forceBody is false, behavior is byte-identical to today. Keep the function pure (no I/O).
   (d) FIX planner.go BuildPlannerSystemPrompt (L128, L142): CRITICAL DISCREPANCY from PRD — the planner currently dispatches on `if format == "auto"` and calls `formatScaffoldBody(format)` with the RAW format string. With +body suffixes, this breaks (auto+body falls through to scaffold dispatch which returns ""). Fix: add `base, _ := splitFormat(format)` before the L142 dispatch; change `if format == "auto"` to `if base == "auto"`; change `formatScaffoldBody(format)` to `formatScaffoldBody(base)`. The planner does NOT get body-forcing (no bodyForceDirective) — only the message-role path does.
4. OUTPUT: Exposes splitFormat(), bodyForceDirective const, and a forceBody-aware buildFormatSystemPrompt() for consumption by S2 (system.go) and S3 (load.go validateFormat). formatScaffoldBody continues to receive the BASE string (unchanged contract — it switches on "conventional"/"gitmoji"/default).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] none beyond inline code comments — format.go and planner.go have no user-facing surface. Update the doc comments on buildFormatSystemPrompt and BuildPlannerSystemPrompt to mention the +body / forceBody behavior.

subtasks.title: system.go: thread forceBody through BuildSystemPrompt + BuildFallbackPrompt (the auto+body special case)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/021_086bbc57a2b2/architecture/format_subsystem.md. system.go BuildSystemPrompt (L102) and BuildFallbackPrompt (L168) currently dispatch on `format != "auto"` (raw string equality). With +body, auto+body would incorrectly match the `!= "auto"` branch and delegate to buildFormatSystemPrompt, losing the examples block. The fix is to parse the base before dispatching.
2. INPUT: splitFormat() and bodyForceDirective from P1.M1.T1.S1. The existing constants: maturePromptHeader, antiReuseProhibition, multilineRuleAllow, multilineRuleSingle, fallbackPromptBody, promptPreamble. The existing helpers: formatScaffoldBody(base), withLocale(s, locale), subjectTargetLine(int).
3. LOGIC:
   (a) BuildSystemPrompt: At the top, `base, forceBody := splitFormat(format)`. Change the early-return dispatch from `if format != "auto"` to `if base != "auto"` — non-auto +body formats delegate to buildFormatSystemPrompt (S1 already handles forceBody internally). For the auto path: when forceBody is true, emit the examples block as today (maturePromptHeader + examples + antiReuseProhibition) but write bodyForceDirective INSTEAD OF the multilineRuleAllow/multilineRuleSingle branch. When forceBody is false, behavior is byte-identical to today. Dispatch formatScaffoldBody(base) (not raw format). The subject-target line follows the rule/directive in both cases.
   (b) BuildFallbackPrompt: `base, forceBody := splitFormat(format)`. Change `if format != "auto"` to `if base != "auto"`. For the auto path: when forceBody is true, append bodyForceDirective after the essence/target line (the new-repo auto+body case). When forceBody is false, byte-identical to today.
   (c) BYTE-IDENTITY GUARANTEE (FR-F1): auto (no suffix) + empty locale MUST be byte-identical to pre-delta. splitFormat("auto") returns ("auto", false); forceBody is false; the assembly paths are unchanged. Verify against the existing TestBuildSystemPrompt_CanonicalExact and TestBuildFallbackPrompt_CanonicalExact tests which must remain GREEN without modification.
4. OUTPUT: BuildSystemPrompt and BuildFallbackPrompt now correctly handle <base>[+body] for all 4 bases (auto/conventional/gitmoji/plain) × 2 suffix states (plain/+body). All 4 downstream call sites (generate.go, decompose/message.go, decompose/planner.go, hook/exec.go) gain +body support automatically since they pass cfg.Format verbatim.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] none — system.go has no user-facing surface. Update doc comments on BuildSystemPrompt and BuildFallbackPrompt to document the +body / forceBody behavior and the byte-identity guarantee.

subtasks.title: load.go: extend validateFormat to the <base>[+body] grammar
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/021_086bbc57a2b2/architecture/format_subsystem.md. load.go L571: validFormats = []string{"auto", "conventional", "gitmoji", "plain"} (the 4 bases). load.go L577: validateFormat(format string) error loops over validFormats and returns fmt.Errorf("invalid format %q (valid: %s)", format, strings.Join(validFormats, ", ")). It is PURE (no I/O), called ONCE at the tail of Load() on the FULLY RESOLVED cfg.Format.
2. INPUT: splitFormat() from P1.M1.T1.S1. The existing validFormats slice (stays the 4 bases — the suffix is grammar, not a mode).
3. LOGIC: Modify validateFormat: `base, forceBody := splitFormat(format)`; validate `base` against the existing validFormats set (same loop); if base is not in validFormats, return an error. This covers +body alone (base="", not in set), bogus+body (base="bogus", not in set), and valid bases with or without +body. Update the error message to name the grammar: e.g. `invalid format %q (valid: <base>[+body], base \u2208 auto, conventional, gitmoji, plain)` — mirroring the existing error shape but surfacing the +body option. The validFormats slice STAYS the 4 bases (it documents the base set).
4. OUTPUT: validateFormat now accepts auto, conventional, gitmoji, plain, AND each with exactly one trailing +body. Rejects +body alone, <base>+body+body (splitFormat returns base="<base>+body", which is not in validFormats), <unknown>+body, <base>+Body (case mismatch — splitFormat is case-sensitive on "+body"), and any other suffix.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] none — validateFormat output is an error string, not a doc surface.
